Spatial residual diagnostics and residual-kriging correction for SDM predictions

Source: R/spatial_bias_reduction.R
restrict_to_aoa.Rd

A small pipeline for the question a pooled decision curve cannot answer: are a model's errors spatially structured, and if so can that structure be turned into a bias-correction surface? Call point_residuals() to attach the signed difference \(y - \hat p\) between observed occurrence and predicted suitability, then reduce_spatial_bias() to run the rest end to end: fit a variogram to the residuals, krige them (optionally with a bootstrap ensemble) onto a prediction grid, and add that correction back onto the prediction raster. Depends on sf, gstat, terra.

Usage

restrict_to_aoa(newdata, aoa, aoa_thresh = 1, crs = sf::st_crs(newdata))

Arguments

newdata

An sf point layer or a terra SpatRaster.

aoa

The AOA as a SpatRaster dissimilarity-index surface (in-AOA where di <= aoa_thresh) or an sf/SpatVector polygon. NULL returns newdata unchanged.

aoa_thresh

In-domain DI threshold for a raster aoa (default 1).

crs

CRS to align a polygon aoa against (the points' CRS).

Value

newdata masked (raster) or filtered (points) to the AOA.

Details

The individual stages - residual_variogram(), residual_krige(), bootstrap_correction() and apply_residual_correction() - are internal and driven by reduce_spatial_bias().

Sign convention throughout: a POSITIVE residual is a site the model UNDER-rates (observed exceeds predicted); a negative residual is one it over-rates.

The correction surface is only trustworthy where the model interpolates, so the kriging stages take an aoa (a dissimilarity-index surface, in-AOA where di <= aoa_thresh, or a polygon) and predict inside it only; outside the AOA no correction is produced. Restrict prediction locations to the area of applicability

The AOA follows the package convention (see aoa_fraction): a raster aoa is a CAST dissimilarity-index (DI) surface, in-AOA where di <= aoa_thresh. A polygon aoa is taken as the in-AOA region directly.
